title: St Pauls (London Views Gold)
descriptionHtml:
One of the first linocuts of the 'London Views' series to be made, this print set the style for many artworks that were to follow it, from 'Fleet Street Apocalypse' and 'Lost Angeles' to the monumental cupola tower in the Bonnefantenmuseum in Maastricht. This print shows the Cathedral Church of St Paul the Apostle in London. Built by Christopher Wren to replace an earlier structure that burnt down during the Great Fire of London in 1666, it occupies the site where legend states King Lud crashed to his death after magically flying there from the city of Bath where he reigned supreme, guarded by his vicious pack of flesh-eating pigs. This legend, however, is not widely believed. Though it is the case that the cathedral is aligned with the point at which the sun rose on Easter Day the year that construction began in 1675. From completion it was the tallest building in London until 1963. Amazing, hey? Don't say you never learn nothing on the internet.

1 colour screen print on gold anodised aluminium foil heat-pressed on 270gsm paper.
Paper size 500mm x 400mm
Print size 292mm x 290mm
From an edition of 88 prints

title: Centre Point (London Views Gold)
descriptionHtml:
'Centre Point' is a skyscraper at the eastern end of Oxford Street in London. It was built amid great controversy between 1963 and 1966. For many years it remained untenanted, earning the nickname 'The Empty Skyscraper'. It has recently been redeveloped, and now contains residential apartments. This print, which also shows the Post Office Tower (now called the BT Tower, opened in 1966), is part of the 'London Views' series, and was printed onto gold foil in 2007.


1 colour screen print on gold anodised aluminium foil heat-pressed on 270gsm paper.
Paper size 495mm x 395mm
Print size 297mm x 195mm
From an edition of 88 prints

title: Gherkin (London Views Gold)
descriptionHtml:
The 'Gherkin', properly known as 30 St Mary Axe, is an office building designed by Norman foster and built between 2001 and 2003. It's much loved by Londoners, something that can't be said about some of its more recently constructed neighbours. Since this print was made the Gherkin has been rendered almost invisible by a plethora of less distinguished creations. So it goes. The print also shows Richard Seifert's nearby NatWest tower, as well as the rather older Tower of London.

1 colour screen print on gold anodised aluminium foil heat-pressed on 270gsm paper.
Paper size 495mm x 395mm
Print size 297mm x 195mm
From an edition of 77 prints

title: Big Ben 2019
descriptionHtml:
This is an edition printed in 2019, taken from the series 'London Views', which is a panorama of London being destroyed by fire and flood carved in lino in a quasi-Mediaeval style. The linocuts from which these screen printed editions are taken were carved in 2006 and once as ever seem deeply apposite, as the United Kingdom sets about an incomprehensible process of self-immolation and destruction. The black is enamel ink, and is very shiny.


Two colour hand-pulled screen print.
Edition of 100.
Print size 340mm x 520mm (approx).
Paper size 420mm x 640mm.


Numbered and signed by the artist.
Blind-embossed with the Slowly Downward Manufactory seal.
